Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment request: Japan residency + audit window + commercial ask — Deal desk escalation

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the ask and the attached security questions. We should aim to keep deals moving but not at the expense of operational risk. My decisions: 

1) Discount: approve up to 30% for year one if customer commits to a 24-month reserved capacity (or 12 months + additional integration/service credits equivalent to the delta). We should avoid a straight 35% concession without additional commitment.

2) Audit window: decline the 72-hour SLA. Approve a compromise of 5 business days for audit requests with the following conditions:
   - Customer must submit a formal audit request form (we will share) and scope must be agreed 72 hours before the start of the audit period.
   - Audits limited to log exports and config snapshots; no live interactive shell access unless separately reviewed and authorized by Legal.

3) Security guardrails: require customer-managed KMS in their VPC for any customer key use, and require read-only, timestamped log exports delivered to a secure S3 bucket in JP region. No raw backups allowed outside JP.

4) Commercial offsets: require either extended term (24 months) or a one-time infra-availability fee equivalent to 5% of the reserved commit in year one.

If Legal (Neha) signs off on the audit carveouts phrasing, we can propose final language and send DocuSign (link below). I'll approve the 30% under those conditions.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Business Ops & Platforms
Redwood Inference
